Aisha says verse 4.6 came about the guardian of orphans: a rich guardian takes no wages from their property, a poor one what is just and reasonable for his labour.
Aisha explains verse 4:3: guardians tempted by an orphan girl's wealth and beauty must give her a fair mahr and treat her justly, or else marry other women.
Aisha explains verses 4.2-3: a guardian drawn to an orphan girl's beauty and wealth may marry her only with a full dowry like her peers', otherwise he marries other women.
Aisha says verse 4.6 came about an orphan's guardian: if he is poor, he may take what is just and reasonable from the orphan's wealth.
Ibn Umar never refused guardianship, Ibn Sirin liked guardians to meet on an orphan's good, Tawus cited verse 2.220, and Ata said guardians provide for orphans from their shares.
Guardians were forbidden to marry orphan girls for their wealth or beauty without a fair dowry, and a poor guardian may take a reasonable wage from the orphan's property.
Aisha said the verse on instructions about women concerns a guardian who keeps an orphan girl sharing his property from marrying, neither marrying her himself nor letting another.
Showing his middle and index fingers, the Prophet said he and the one who looks after an orphan will be like this in Paradise.
The Prophet said he and the one who looks after an orphan will be in Paradise like his two joined fingers.
Aisha explained the verse on orphan girls: guardians drawn by their wealth and beauty were forbidden to marry them with less than a full Mahr.
